      WHY SGLN?

      1. Provides exposure through ETC securities whose value is linked to the price of gold
      2. Linked to physical gold held for iShares Physical Metals plc
      3. Valued based on the LBMA gold price
      4. Compliant with Shariah investment principles

      INVESTMENT OBJECTIVE

      The objective is for the value of the product to reflect, at any given time, the price of gold. The product represents an exchange traded commodity issued by iShares Physical Metals plc which is linked to the performance of gold physically held for the iShares Physical Metals plc. Each exchange traded commodity corresponds to a proportion of the gold held for the iShares Physical Metals plc. Changes in the value of the exchange traded commodity correspond directly to changes in the price of gold, save that the value of the securities is also impacted by fees

      Important Information: Capital at Risk. The value of investments and the income from them can fall as well as rise and are not guaranteed. Investors may not get back the amount originally invested.

      Important Information: The value of your investment will vary and your initial investment amount cannot be guaranteed, The securities issued by iShares Physical Metals plc are limited recourse obligations which are payable solely out of the underlying secured property. If the secured property is insufficient any outstanding claims will remain unpaid. ETCs will seek exposure to a limited number of market sectors. Compared to investments which spread investment risk more generally through a variety of sectors, price movements may have a greater effect on the overall value of the investment. Precious metal prices are generally more volatile than most other asset classes, making investments riskier and more complex than other investments.
      ETCs trade on exchanges like securities and are bought and sold at market prices which may be different to the net asset values of the ETCs.

      The index is not a benchmark within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2016/1011.

      Key Risks

      The prices of commodities tend to experience greater variations than other asset classes (e.g. equities or fixed income securities). Investments in commodities are therefore potentially riskier than other types of investments.Counterparty Risk: The insolvency of any institutions providing services such as safekeeping of assets or acting as counterparty to derivatives or other instruments, may expose the Product to financial loss.Issuer Default Risk: The issuer may fail to perform or comply with one or more of its material obligations, including payment of sums due and delivery of any metal due, which may expose the Product to financial loss.
